inline:The target's stated cross-city modulator (built density and impervious surface fraction) fails as the single best explanation for why the nocturnal UHI gap is larger in some cities than in others, because aridity/humidity is a stronger modulator that the target omits.
The problem asks for the single mechanism that best explains why the night-time gap is larger in some cities than in others. The target answers 'built density and impervious surface fraction.' But the dominant cross-city modulator of a thermal-mass release story is ambient humidity/aridity: in humid cities abundant rural atmospheric water vapor emits longwave radiation back to the surface at night, narrowing the urban-rural cooling-rate gap; in arid cities dry rural air emits far less longwave, so the countryside cools rapidly by radiative loss and the nocturnal gap is much larger for the same thermal mass. By attributing the gap to density/imperviousness instead, the target misidentifies the best cross-city mechanism.
